about: Jesus speaks of keeping His word, promises the Holy Spirit, and gives His disciples peace before His departure.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word, and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and will make Our abode with him. He who does not love Me does not keep My words. And the word which you have heard is not Mine, but belongs to the Father who sent Me. These things I have spoken to you, abiding with you. But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, He will teach you all things and remind you of everything I have said to you. Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid. You have heard that I said to you: I go away, and I come to you. If you loved Me, you would indeed be glad because I go to the Father, for the Father is greater than I. And now I have told you before it comes to pass, that when it has come to pass you may believe. I will not speak much more with you. For the prince of this world is coming, and in Me he has nothing. But I do as the Father commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father.

a.g: Let your heart not be troubled
For the prince of this world is coming

ex.w025: Here mansiónem apud eum faciémus means “We will make Our abode with him”: the Father and the Son promise to dwell with the person who loves Jesus.
ex.w038: Here the noun sermónem takes the accusative case of the following relative quem. Valla cites this sentence as an example of that construction. Meus still means “Mine” in the statement about the word.
ex.w076: Díxero is future perfect, “I will have said.” It views the teaching of Jesus from the time when the Spirit brings it to mind, when all of it will already have been spoken. It does not mean that His teaching has yet to begin.
ex.w148: Quidquam is the neuter “anything,” not “anyone.” With non it states that the prince of this world has nothing in Jesus and no hold over Him.
